summary: Extended the approved Clinical Glass system across the complete OncoReady experience, added accessible one-time landing reveals and a buyer-oriented SaaS model, removed costly scroll treatments, and preserved the deterministic Maria journey and caregiver privacy boundary.

commands: npx vitest run tests/smoke.test.ts tests/component.test.tsx tests/continuity-field.test.tsx tests/scroll-reveal.test.tsx
python3 scripts/agentctl.py scope check UI-001 frontend
tests.notes: TypeScript completed successfully. The production Vite build passed twice; the latest build transformed 8,481 modules in 3m38s. Focused Vitest passed 4 files and 14 tests. Playwright passed all 3 UI-001 scenarios: one-time reveal/SaaS positioning/responsive overflow and performance-style checks; system reduced-motion final-state behavior; and all staff routes plus the complete Maria journey and caregiver clinical-data exclusion. Visual review passed the landing roles/SaaS sections and patient/staff workspaces.

notes_for_next_agent: The reveal primitive uses IntersectionObserver progressive enhancement, unobserves completed targets, promotes focused content immediately, and renders final content without observer support or under either reduced-motion source.
The SaaS section states the buyer, subscribed capability, configuration shape, and expansion path without pricing, fabricated integrations, or demo/prototype framing.
Clinical Glass tokens now cover public, gateway, patient, staff, caregiver, system, modal, navigation, and mobile-dock surfaces while preserving operational labels and workflow semantics.

Fixed body backgrounds, broad repeated blur, the staff nested vertical scroller, and eager live-map mounting were removed or bounded; the document owns workspace scrolling and the stable map fallback remains available.
Caregiver rendering remains transportation-only, and browser coverage confirms clinical symptom text is absent after the staff resolution flow.
